public_rationale: The cited audit establishes citation problems in Deep Research-generated reports. It does not establish the additional step Marcus predicts: an error entering scientific literature as substantive content. No qualifying dated publication case was verified. With no deadline, the forecast remains open.
limitations: This assessment uses the contextual meaning of infected as erroneous contamination.
The search cannot prove that qualifying publications do not exist.
The citation audit is a preprint and uses an operational test for likely fabricated URLs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The scientific literature itself, not just models, will be infected by Deep Research output.

statement.excerpt: And it’s not just the models that will be infected, but the scientific literature itself.
statement.document_title: Deep Research, Deep Bullshit, and the potential (model) collapse of science

our_interpretation: Infected means factual or citation errors from OpenAI Deep Research being incorporated into scientific publications as substantive content.
The surrounding text makes erroneous contamination the ordinary reading; harmless assistance or a disclosed outline alone does not satisfy it.
An evaluation publishing labelled examples of errors is not itself an instance of contamination.
This sentence supplies no minimum prevalence, so one authenticated contamination case can establish the literature component.
criteria.support_condition: At least one published scientific assertion or reference is demonstrably erroneous and traceable to OpenAI Deep Research output incorporated into the publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence rules out the predicted contamination pathway. Clean publications or failure to find a case by an unstated deadline are insufficient.

evidence.explanation: The audit reports citation-URL failures in generated research reports, using URL resolution and archival checks. It does not demonstrate that any such citation was subsequently incorporated as a reference in a scientific publication.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A published scientific paper containing a verified error, with author records or an independent investigation tracing that error specifically to OpenAI Deep Research output.
